paper_metadata.title: High-strength and low-modulus Ti–13Nb–7Sn–4Mo with β + α″ + α structure fabricated by cold rolling and aging treatment

evidence.quote: In this study, the structure and mechanical properties of the previously developed metastable Ti–13Nb–7Sn–4Mo (TNSM) alloy with low elastic modulus (54 GPa) [12] were investigated through cold rolling and aging treatment under various conditions.

In this study, the mechanical properties of Ti–13Nb–7Sn–4Mo (wt%) was improved through 90% cold rolling and subsequent aging treatment under different aging temperatures (500, 550, and 600°C) and times (30, 60, and 120 min).

The TNSM alloy was prepared from Ti (99.7 wt% pure), Nb (99.95 wt% pure), Sn (99.9 wt% pure), and Mo (99.95 wt% pure) using a commercial arc-melting vacuum pressure casting system (A-028, DAWN SHINE, Taiwan). The alloy ingots were flipped and re-melted five times for chemical homogeneity.
The TNSM alloy was cold rolled using a double rolling machine with a roll diameter of 15 cm (5TSB, Jong Yih Co., Taiwan).

The as-cast TNSM alloy (TNSM-1) exhibited β equiaxed grains.
After 90% cold rolling, the grains of TNSM-2 alloy were elongated along the rolling direction (horizontal).
After solution treatment, TNSM-3 alloy exhibited smaller equiaxed β grains than TNSM-1, which was attributed to the recrystallization of the alloy during solution treatment.
After aging treatment, equiaxed β grains and a small amount of fine needle-like α" structure (yellow arrow) could be observed in the OM images (TNSM-4 to TNSM-8).

The equiaxed grains were found in the alloy under low magnification image [Fig. 3(a) and (b)].
The bending strength of as-cast TNSM (TNSM-1) alloy was 1154.6 MPa.
Subsequent 90% cold rolling, the bending strength of TNSM-2 alloy increased to 1230.4 MPa, which was attributed to the strain hardening caused by cold rolling.

However, the bending strength of TNSM-3 alloy decreased to 1091.9 MPa after solution treatment, which might be related to the elimination of the dislocation in the cold-rolled alloy or the excessive growth of β grains during the solution treatment.
Among them, TNSM-4 showed the greatest bending strength (1424.3 MPa).

TNSM-2 alloy slightly decreased from 54.7 GPa (TNSM-1) to 52.8 GPa, which could result from the stress-induced α″ martensitic transformation (β → α″) occurred during the cold-rolling process.
After solution treatment, the elastic modulus of TNSM-3 increased to 54.2 GPa due to the volume fraction of the α″ phase in TNSM-3 was decreased from 31 to 21%.
When the aging temperature increased from 500 to 600°C for 120 min, the elastic modulus of the alloy increased from 68.9 GPa (TNSM-4) to 73.4 GPa (TNSM-6)

When the aging temperature increased from 500 to 600°C for 120 min, the elastic modulus of the alloy increased from 68.9 GPa (TNSM-4) to 73.4 GPa (TNSM-6), which is related to the increasing volume fraction of the α phase from 7 to 13%.

With reducing the aging time to 60 min, the elastic modulus of TNSM-7 alloy dropped significantly to 60.3 GPa, which may be attributed to the decrease of the volume fraction and the grain size of the α phase.
Moreover, the elastic modulus of TNSM-8 alloy further decreased to 58.5 GPa when the aging time was shortened to 30 min.

The 90% cold-rolled sample (TNSM-2) exhibited a β + α″ dual-phase structure, which was attributed to the stress-induced martensitic transformation during the cold-rolling process.
After aging treatments, the bending strengths of TNSM alloys enhanced significantly, probably attributed to the precipitation of the α phase.

On the contrary, the bending strengths of TNSM-6 and TNSM-7 were significantly lower than those of the other aged alloys, which could be correlated with the overaging. Overaging may reduce the strength of the alloy and also cause a substantial increase in the elastic modulus.
